tool_tier: Claude subscription — not the free or public tier
how: Pair-programmed notebook implementation, debugging, lint/CI fixes, git housekeeping (merges/conflicts), and editorial passes on reader-facing prose.
why: To work through unfamiliar parts of the stack step by step as a learning partner rather than a black box, and to move faster through mechanical work so more time went to modeling/analysis calls.
lede: I'm Yai Torres, one of four people on this GRAD 50400 project (Group 14). This page is my individual pair-programming disclosure under the course's AI Tool Use Policy, which asks for exactly which tools were used and their tier, the history of each exchange, and how and why each tool was used — answered below, then backed by a real timeline instead of a paraphrase.
methodology_note: The 50 commits are every commit carrying a Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 trailer. The 26 threads are the actual coding sessions behind them — some run directly on main/a feature branch in this checkout, others in a git worktree under a claude/* branch — matched to each commit by timestamp (a commit is attributed to the thread whose active window contains it). I'm the author and committer of record on every commit: I decided what to build, which fix to take, and when a section was actually done. Quoted lines are the thread's own opening message, lightly trimmed for length; full transcripts are linked, not reconstructed dialogue. See the published report for the project itself, or its closing "AI usage appendix" for the team's external chat-thread disclosures (Perplexity, Claude.ai) covering project planning and exploration rather than pair-programming.
footer_note: Threads sourced from local Claude Code session logs (17 in this checkout, 9 run inside git worktrees) covering this repository; commits from git log --all --grep="Co-Authored-By: Claude". Each commit is attributed to the thread whose active time window contains it, except two threads (Aug 5, Aug 7) whose commits merged days later via PR — those list their commit manually rather than by timestamp window. Full prompt/response transcripts for all 26 threads are in docs/ai/logs/. Regenerate after adding threads or commits with uv run python scripts/toolkit.py ai-disclosure ytorresv.
